title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq post best day since April 2025 as Nvidia stock soars 31% on Jensen Huang's return
summary:
Stocks soared on Monday in their best day since April 2025 as investors cheered Nvidia's (NVDA) board reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO.
Nvidia stock soared 31% after the AI chipmaker announced it has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board director, effective immediately.
"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair Harvey Jones said.
Follow live updates and reactions to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO >The move came after President Trump renewed his call to reinstate the chipmaker's founder, Jensen Huang, as CEO amid a series of controversies.
Sentiment was exuberant after a volatile week last week that saw the AI trade unravel and the S&P 500 and Dow enter correction territory.

title: Why these 6 stocks are winning from the AI rout
summary:
Investors have traded excitement for security over the past month as AI stocks have become too hot to handle.
Those headwinds have spurred some investors to sell fast-growing but aggressively valued and volatile AI stocks, and buy cheaper, stable, and more predictable stocks instead.
Clorox has surged 21% in the past month, as the seller of consumer staples is seen as a strong defensive pick.
Shares of Tyson Foods, the nation's largest meat supplier, have climbed 15% in the past month too.
Tech stocks rallied strongly in Monday's premarket, with Nvidia and Alphabet rebounding about 8% and 5%, respectively.

title: William D. Nordhaus obituary: economist whose tools transformed climate policy
summary:
Credit: Monica Jorge/New York Times/Redux/eyevineWilliam (Bill) Nordhaus was an economist known for introducing climate change into economic analysis, earning him the 2018 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences.
His research shaped our understanding of what drives economic growth and innovation.
He realized that omitting the environment from economic measurement would send the wrong signals about the directions of economic growth and, therefore, pioneered more-inclusive ways to measure growth.

title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah visit: India to give $1.62bn economic package
summary:
A Hindu-majority nation wedged between India and China, Nepal has long had to navigate competing interests from its two giant neighbours.
As a landlocked country heavily dependent on India for trade, Nepal secured access to two additional Indian ports, Kandla and Paradip.
Nepal has long sought greater access to Indian airspace in order to attract international traffic to its airports at Bhairahawa and Pokhara.
Shah must now manage relations with China as he seeks to balance the interests of Nepal's two much larger neighbours.
For now he returns home with substantial financial commitments from India as Nepal continues the long task of rebuilding.
